title: Four jobs of an analytical paragraph
statement: Mark an analytical paragraph on four jobs, each checked alone: a claim answering the question, a quotation, what a quoted word suggests, and a link back to the question.
example: Only one of the four jobs, the quotation, is settled in code; the judge answers a separate question for each of the other three.
detail: A 3D version's paragraph task was brought into the lesson engine as its rules and wording, with its four jobs: point, evidence, analysis and link (`g9/transformer/src/glue/threejs-archivist.js`). Evidence is settled in code, as words quoted from the text exactly or nearly, and the judge answers a separate question for each of the other three jobs. A paragraph is secure only when all four hold, and a job counts as missing only on a confident no.
against: When the lesson engine's own claim-evidence-reasoning block used this task, it took only the next step, never the verdict, so the answer stayed unmarked (`g9/transformer/v02/QA.md`, lines 32-33). The next-step check has five seed cases, obvious ones only, so how well the judge applies the standard to real paragraphs is not measured, and no lesson has yet been used by a student (`g9/transformer/test/calibration/cer-frame.next-step.json`, `g9/transformer/README.md`).
